findings.title: File answer takes length/ETag/Last-Modified from one stat and the body from a later open, so a file replaced in between is sent truncated under the old validators
findings.description: respond() calls FileResourceResolver.stat(path) (length L1, mtime M1, ETag from them) and only later r.open(path) (a second, independent check and FileInputStream). If the file is swapped between the two (typical when a deploy replaces bundle.js with mv/cp while traffic is live) and the new file is larger (L2 > L1), sendBody(200, in, 0, L1) commits Content-Length L1, copies exactly L1 bytes of the NEW file, and completes normally: the client receives a well-framed but truncated body labelled with the OLD ETag/Last-Modified (and any immutable/max-age policy), and caches it. If L2 < L1 the copy aborts mid-body. The re-check inside open() only compares canonical paths, not size/mtime, so it does not catch this.
findings.suggested_fix: After r.open(path) re-stat (or use FileInputStream.getChannel().size() plus a fresh lastModified) and, if length or mtime differs from the first stat, close the stream and recompute length/tag/seconds (retry once) or answer 503 without validators.

findings.title: Directory listing links files whose names StaticPath then refuses with 400
findings.description: render() lists every non-dot, non-link entry. A file named 'a%2eb' or 'x%2fy' (or one containing a backslash) is emitted as href 'a%252eb'; the follow-up request decodes once to 'a%2eb', which StaticPath.check rejects because the decoded segment still contains '%2e' (StaticPath.java:35), so the listed link answers 400 instead of the file. No traversal, only a listing/serving mismatch.
findings.suggested_fix: Skip entries in render() for which StaticPath.check(PercentDecoder.percentEncode(name, "-._~")) != 0.
